```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(macodgent)
library(MASS)
```

# Background

Part 2 ("Routine Analysis Techniques") of the column *Exploring Medical Data
Science with R* covers eight chapters: meeting the data, preprocessing,
quantitative / qualitative description, conventional regression, survival
analysis, advanced regression, and advanced survival analysis. Each section
scatters reusable analysis actions. `macodgent` distils those actions into a
uniform set of `mc_*` functions that always return a tidy `data.frame`.

# 1. Data overview and mode

```{r}
mc_inspect(birthwt)[1:6, ]
mc_mode(c(1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6))
```

# 2. Quantitative description (flagship: 20 metrics at once)

```{r}
mc_desc_quant(birthwt, vars = c("age", "lwt", "bwt"))
```

# 3. Univariate screen -> multivariable logistic

```{r}
sc <- mc_logistic_screen(birthwt, y = "low",
  x_vars = c("age", "lwt", "race", "smoke", "ht", "ui"))
sc$univariate
```

# 4. Survival analysis

```{r}
fit <- mc_cox(survival::lung, survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog)
fit$forest
```

# 5. Restricted cubic spline (self-built basis)

```{r}
rcs <- mc_rcs(birthwt, x = "age", y = "bwt", nk = 3)
rcs$plot
```

The mapping between each function and the chapters of Part 2 is listed in the
module table of `README.md`.
